mainTopic: Who removes impurity from the מקדש and who may enter the היכל for repairs; the cases behind רבי שמעון's principle; the end of מסכת עירובין.
overview: רבי יוחנן shows that רבי שמעון בן ננס and רבי עקיבא learn their dispute about removing a שרץ from the מקדש from the same פסוק. In that פסוק, כהנים carried impurity out of the היכל and handed it to לויים in the courtyard. רבי שמעון בן ננס reads the handoff as proof that the עזרה needs no removal. רבי עקיבא reads it as a way to spare the כהנים from extra impurity. A ברייתא then teaches that anyone may enter the היכל to build, repair, or remove impurity: כהנים first, then לויים, then ישראלים, but only if they are טהור. רב כהנא's ברייתא disagrees and sends in even a טמא or blemished כהן before any ישראל. The גמרא asks whether a טמא or a בעל מום should go first. רב and רבי אלעזר give opposite answers, and the question is not decided. Next, the גמרא shows which cases רבי שמעון's principle in the משנה refers to: the person just outside the תחום, and the broken harp string, where only a bow (a שבות) is allowed and not a knot. The amud ends with the הדרן, completing מסכת עירובין.

steps.title: Both opinions come from the same verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says רבי שמעון בן ננס and רבי עקיבא both learn their positions from one פסוק about חזקיהו's cleansing of the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Both of them learned from the same verse: 'The כהנים came into the inner part of the House of ה׳ to purify it. They brought out all the impurity they found in the היכל of ה׳ to the courtyard of the House of ה׳. Then the לויים took it to carry it out to the brook of קדרון, outside.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן quotes the shared source text for the dispute from the משנה. This sets up the next two steps, where the גמרא explains how each side reads it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse describes a two-stage removal. First, כהנים carry the impurity from inside the היכל out to the courtyard (the עזרה). Then לויים take it from the courtyard to נחל קדרון. The whole dispute hinges on what that handoff in the courtyard means.

keyTerms.meaning: the Sanctuary building, the inner holy area
the courtyard of the Temple (the עזרה)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Both of them' does not mean רבי יוחנן and someone else. It refers to the two תנאים of the משנה, רבי שמעון בן ננס and רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
And both of them expounded one verse:
phrases.notes: Both = רבי שמעון בן ננס and רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: "And the priests came into the inner part of the House of God
to purify it, and they brought out all the impurity
that they found in the Sanctuary of God
to the courtyard of the House of God,
and the Levites received it to take it out
to the brook of Kidron, outside." (II Chronicles 29:16)

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, וּשְׁנֵיהֶם מִקְרָא אֶחָד דָּרְשׁוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this passage by grounding the משנה's dispute in a shared verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute between רבי שמעון בן ננס and רבי עקיבא is a dispute about how to read one פסוק.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the argument is not about different sources but about interpreting one event, the handoff from כהנים to לויים.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן ננס: the switch shows the courtyard needs no removal
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן ננס reads the change to לויים in the עזרה as proof that impurity in the courtyard is not something the כהנים must remove.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage holds: since the job switched to the לויים once it reached the עזרה, that shows there is no requirement to remove impurity from the עזרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי שמעון בן ננס reads the verse. In his view, the handoff in the courtyard shows that the obligation to remove impurity ended there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the courtyard required removal just like the היכל, the כהנים would have kept carrying it out. The fact that a different group took over shows that the courtyard is outside the zone where removal is required. That fits his view in the משנה: remove only from the היכל, the אולם, and between the אולם and the מזבח.

phrases.english: One Sage holds:
since it was changed in the courtyard to the Levites,
there is no [requirement to remove] impurity in the courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first side's reading of the verse quoted in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The switch to לויים in the עזרה shows that removing impurity from the courtyard is not required.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why רבי שמעון בן ננס limits the removal to the inner areas of the מקדש.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the switch only avoids making priests impure
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא reads the handoff as practical: כהנים carried it only where לויים could not go, and once לויים could take over, כהנים stopped defiling themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other Sage holds: as long as the לויים could not do it, the כהנים carried it out. Once the לויים could do it, the כהנים no longer made themselves impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי עקיבא's reading of the same verse. For him, the switch says nothing about whether the courtyard needs removal. It only tells us who should do the carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לויים may not enter the היכל, so inside it only כהנים could carry the impurity. In the עזרה, where לויים are allowed, the job passed to them so that כהנים would not stay in contact with impurity longer than necessary. The removal itself continued through the courtyard, which fits רבי עקיבא's view that impurity must be removed from any place where entering impure carries כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: up to where / as long as

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree on the facts of the פסוק. רבי שמעון בן ננס says the handoff shows the עזרה needs no removal. רבי עקיבא says the handoff only spared the כהנים, and removal from the עזרה is still required.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי עקיבא holds the courtyard needs no removal. In his reading, the impurity still had to go all the way out. It simply switched carriers.

phrases.english: And the other Sage holds:
up to where it is not possible with Levites,
priests take it out.
Now that it is possible with Levites,
priests no longer make themselves impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the opposing reading of the same verse, in contrast to step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The switch to לויים was only to avoid unnecessary impurity for כהנים, so the obligation to remove continues through the עזרה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dispute is whether the handoff in the עזרה marks the end of the obligation to remove or just a change in who carries.
steps.whyThisMatters: It introduces a key principle: כהנים should avoid contact with impurity beyond what is necessary.

steps.title: Anyone may enter the Sanctuary for repairs or removing impurity, with priests preferred
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that anyone may enter the היכל to build, repair, or remove impurity. The מצוה is to use כהנים, then לויים, then ישראלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Everyone may enter the היכל to build, to repair, or to remove impurity, but the מצוה is to use כהנים. If no כהנים are there, לויים enter. If no לויים are there, ישראלים enter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on a related question: who is allowed into the היכל for necessary work like building, repairs, or removing impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally only כהנים may enter the היכל. For necessary work, the ברייתא allows anyone, but it sets an order of preference: כהנים first, then לויים, then ישראלים. This fits the theme of the previous steps, that who does the job matters, here in terms of holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: but the preferred מצוה is with priests

steps.confusionAlert: 'Everyone may enter' does not mean any order is fine. It means a לוי or ישראל is allowed in only when no one higher in the order is available.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Everyone may enter the Sanctuary
to build, to repair, and to take out the impurity,
but the מצוה is with priests.
If there are no priests there,
Levites enter;
if there are no Levites there,
Israelites enter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the verse-based dispute to a ברייתא about who may enter the היכל for necessary work.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone may enter the היכל for building, repair, or removing impurity, with the order of preference כהנים, then לויים, then ישראלים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא sets up the discussion that follows about how far this permission extends.

steps.title: Only people who are pure may enter
steps.stepSummary: Whichever group enters, they may do so only if they are טהור, never if they are טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: In both cases: if they are pure, yes; if they are impure, no.
steps.whatsHappening: This line adds a limit to the ברייתא's permission. Whoever enters, whether לויים or ישראלים, must be ritually pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lowering the bar on lineage (letting a non-כהן in) does not lower the bar on purity. Entering the היכל while impure stays forbidden even for necessary work. Purity is required no matter who goes in.

keyTerms.meaning: in both cases / this and that

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא relaxes who may enter the היכל for necessary work, in a set order. It does not relax purity: only people who are טהור may enter.

phrases.english: And in both cases,
phrases.notes: This line is in Aramaic, so it may be the גמרא's clarifying addition to the ברייתא.

phrases.english: if pure, yes [they may enter];
if impure, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי, טְהוֹרִין — אִין, טְמֵאִין — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the permission given in step 4 by requiring purity.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever enters the היכל for necessary work must be טהור. Those who are טמא may not enter.

steps.title: רב כהנא's ברייתא opens with a possible thought about blemished priests
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says רב כהנא supports כהנים, and quotes his ברייתא. It begins with a possible thought: since the פסוק forbids a בעל מום from approaching the פרוכת, maybe blemished כהנים cannot even enter to make gold plating.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: רב כהנא supports כהנים, since he taught: Because it says 'Only he shall not go in to the curtain,' I might think that blemished כהנים may not enter the area between the אולם and the מזבח to hammer out gold plates.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that gives a different ranking from the one in Steps 4-5. This line only sets up a possible thought (יכול), and the next step will reject it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק bars a blemished כהן from serving near the פרוכת and the מזבח. The ברייתא first guesses that this ban also covers non-service work like making gold plating. רב הונא's comment tells us ahead of time that the ruling will favor כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: the holy area between the Entrance Hall and the outer מזבח
'I might have thought', which introduces a possible idea that is about to be rejected

steps.confusionAlert: רב כהנא was himself a כהן. That is why רב הונא remarks that he 'supports כהנים': his ברייתא gives even lesser כהנים priority over ישראלים. The word כהנא here is a name, not a description of the ruling.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Rav Kahana supports priests,
phrases.notes: רב כהנא was a priest himself.

phrases.english: as Rav Kahana taught:
Since it is stated
'Only he shall not go in to the curtain' (Vayikra 21:23),

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל לֹא יְהוּ כֹּהֲנִים בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין
phrases.english: I might think that blemished priests should not
enter between the Entrance Hall and the altar
to make beaten gold plates.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: רַב כָּהֲנָא מְסַיַּיע כָּהֲנֵי, דְּתָנֵי רַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second ברייתא with a different view on who may enter for repairs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening possible thought: maybe blemished כהנים may not enter even to make plating.

steps.title: The word 'only' divides the rule: best people first, others if needed
steps.stepSummary: The word אך teaches a division. Ideally unblemished and טהור כהנים do the work. If none are available, blemished or טמא כהנים may enter.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'only' to make a distinction. The מצוה is done with unblemished ones, but if there are none, blemished ones enter. The מצוה is done with pure ones, but if there are none, impure ones enter.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the possible thought from Step 6. It uses the limiting word אך to allow blemished or טמא כהנים to enter when better ones are not available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אך is read as a 'limiting' word: the ban on blemished כהנים is not total. It sets an order of preference. Unblemished and טהור come first, and the others are a fallback. The same pattern is then applied to טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the verse teaches', which introduces the actual lesson
'only', a word that limits or divides a rule

phrases.english: The verse teaches 'only', which makes a distinction:
the מצוה is with unblemished ones;

phrases.aramaic: אֵין שָׁם תְּמִימִים — נִכְנָסִין בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין.
phrases.english: if there are no unblemished ones there, blemished ones enter.
The מצוה is with pure ones;
if there are no pure ones there, impure ones enter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the possible thought of Step 6 using the word אך.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unblemished and טהור כהנים come first. If there are none, blemished or טמא כהנים may enter.

steps.title: Either way, only priests may enter, not Israelites
steps.stepSummary: In both fallback cases, only כהנים may enter, not ישראלים. So a טמא כהן is preferred over a טהור ישראל. This is how רב כהנא 'supports כהנים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: In both cases: כהנים, yes. ישראלים, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא's ברייתא ends by stating its bottom line: the fallback goes to lesser כהנים, never to ישראלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ברייתא (Steps 4-5) allowed ישראלים in, but only if טהור. רב כהנא's ברייתא instead sends in a טמא or blemished כהן before any ישראל. This explains רב הונא's remark in Step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: 'this and that', meaning in both cases

steps.whatToRemember: רב כהנא's ruling: a lesser כהן (טמא or בעל מום) goes before any ישראל. This contrasts with the earlier ברייתא, which allowed a טהור ישראל but never anyone טמא.

phrases.english: In both cases,
priests, yes;
Israelites, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי, כֹּהֲנִים — אִין, יִשְׂרְאֵלִים — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the practical result of the ruling in Step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only כהנים, even lesser ones, may enter. ישראלים may not.

steps.title: Impure priest or blemished priest: who goes first?
steps.stepSummary: The scholars ask: if the only choices are a טמא כהן and a blemished כהן, which one should enter?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: an impure one and a blemished one, which of them enters?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question that grows out of רב כהנא's ruling. It sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא allowed both a טמא and a בעל מום as fallbacks, but he did not rank them against each other. The question asks which flaw is less serious.

keyTerms.meaning: 'it was asked of them', which introduces a question the scholars raised

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
an impure one and a blemished one,
which of them enters?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a gap left open by רב כהנא's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which flaw ranks lower: טומאה or a מום?

steps.title: רב: the impure priest goes in
steps.stepSummary: רב says the טמא enters, because טומאה is permitted for communal offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: The impure one enters, because he is permitted in communal service.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer: the טמא כהן should go in first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the whole community is טמא, טמא כהנים may bring the communal קרבנות. A בעל מום can never serve. So טומאה is the smaller problem.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi said in the name of Rav:
The impure one enters,
since he was permitted in communal service.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב: טָמֵא נִכְנָס
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The טמא goes first, since טומאה can be permitted for communal service.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the blemished priest goes in
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the בעל מום enters, because he may still eat קדשים. The question is left unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: The blemished one enters, because he is permitted to eat consecrated food.
steps.whatsHappening: A second, opposite answer to the same question. The גמרא does not decide between the two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished כהן keeps his holiness and may eat קדשים, while a טמא may not. רבי אלעזר judges by personal status, and רב judges by permission to do service.
steps.whatToRemember: רב: טמא first (based on service). רבי אלעזר: בעל מום first (based on eating קדשים). No final ruling is given.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
The blemished one enters,
since he was permitted to eat consecrated food.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: בַּעַל מוּם נִכְנָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב's answer in Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בעל מום goes first, since he may still eat קדשים.

steps.title: Which case is רבי שמעון's principle about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line from רבי שמעון (that whatever the חכמים permitted was really yours to begin with) and asks which ruling he is referring to.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'רבי שמעון says' and so on. Where is רבי שמעון standing (what is he referring to)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and opens a new topic. It asks what earlier case רבי שמעון's general principle is built on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון states a general principle without naming a case. The גמרא wants to find which earlier משנה it explains.

keyTerms.meaning: 'etc.', which points to the rest of the משנה's line
'where is he standing?', meaning which case he is referring to

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says, etc.
Where is Rabbi Shimon standing (to what is he referring)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה and starts a new topic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which earlier ruling is רבי שמעון's principle referring to?

steps.title: It refers to someone just outside the תחום
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון refers to the משנה about someone caught outside the תחום when שבת began. He allows coming in from as far as fifteen אמות, because the surveyors mark the limit short of the full distance.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is referring to there, as we learned: One for whom it got dark outside the תחום may not enter even one אמה. רבי שמעון says: Even fifteen אמות, he may enter, because the surveyors do not mark the exact measure, on account of those who make mistakes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 12. It identifies the source case for רבי שמעון's principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The boundary markers are placed inside the true 2000 אמות so that people who make mistakes stay safe. So the person 'outside' the marker is really still inside his own real תחום. That is what 'they only permitted you what is yours' means.

keyTerms.meaning: measure exactly to the full limit

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון's leniency is not a real היתר to cross the תחום. The person never truly left his own permitted area.

phrases.english: He is referring to there, as we learned:
one for whom it got dark outside the Shabbat limit,
even one cubit, he may not enter.
Rabbi Shimon says:
even fifteen cubits, he may enter,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין הַמָּשׁוֹחוֹת מְמַצְּעִין אֶת הַמִּדּוֹת
phrases.english: because the surveyors do not mark the full exact measurement
because of those who err.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It refers to the משנה about someone fifteen אמות past the marked תחום.

steps.title: The dispute over entering from fifteen אמות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer about the תחום case. The תנא קמא says the person may not come in, and רבי שמעון says he may.
steps.simpleTranslation: In that case the first תנא said he may not enter, and רבי שמעון answered him: he may enter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the answer from the last step. It names the two sides of the תחום argument that רבי שמעון's principle was responding to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא forbids coming back in from fifteen אמות outside the marked line. רבי שמעון permits it, because the surveyors mark the line short of the real limit. So the person is really still inside his true תחום, and the 'leniency' was his to begin with.

keyTerms.meaning: The first (anonymous) opinion in the משנה

phrases.english: where the first tanna said: he may not enter,
and Rabbi Shimon said to him: he may enter.
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון's reason is that whatever the חכמים 'permitted' here was really his by right.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Direct continuation of step 13's answer. It finishes identifying the dispute.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The principle 'whatever they permitted was yours' refers to the תחום case, where רבי שמעון disagrees with the תנא קמא and lets the person enter.

steps.title: Which case does 'they only permitted שבות' refer to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of רבי שמעון in the משנה, 'they only permitted you things that are שבות,' and asks which ruling it is about.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For they permitted you only things forbidden because of שבות.' Where is this standing? (Which case is it talking about?)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second half of רבי שמעון's statement and asks what case it refers to. This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's statement in the משנה is general and does not name a case. The גמרא wants to find the specific ruling where the rule 'only rabbinic prohibitions were relaxed' makes a practical difference.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic שבת prohibition (not a Torah one)
Where is it standing? Which case does it refer to?

phrases.english: For they did not permit you
except things forbidden due to a rabbinic decree.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: Where is this standing (which case)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 12. After placing the first half of רבי שמעון's statement, the גמרא now places the second half.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which earlier ruling in the משנה is רבי שמעון's 'only שבות was permitted' principle aimed at?

steps.title: It refers to the broken harp string in the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: The answer is the case of a harp string that snapped on שבת in the מקדש. The תנא קמא lets one tie it, and רבי שמעון allows only a bow.
steps.simpleTranslation: It stands there, where the first תנא said 'he ties it,' and רבי שמעון said to him 'he makes a bow with it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון's rule is aimed at the harp-string case from the earlier משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides allow some fix in the מקדש. The argument is about how far the permission goes. The תנא קמא allows a real knot, but רבי שמעון limits it to a bow, which is less severe.

keyTerms.meaning: He ties it with a real knot
He ties it with a bow (a loop knot)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not get mixed up: in the תחום case רבי שמעון is the lenient one, but here he is the strict one. Both come from the same idea: the חכמים never truly relaxed anything beyond rabbinic level.

phrases.english: It stands there,
where the first tanna said: he ties it with a knot.
phrases.notes: About a harp string in the מקדש that broke on שבת.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon said to him: he forms a bow.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The principle refers to the harp-string dispute: tying a knot (תנא קמא) versus only making a bow (רבי שמעון).

steps.title: Why a bow is allowed but a knot is not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבי שמעון's logic. A bow can never bring a חטאת, so the רבנן permitted it. A knot can bring a חטאת, so they did not permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bow, which cannot bring one to liability for a חטאת, the רבנן permitted. A knot, which can bring one to liability for a חטאת, the רבנן did not permit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the reasoning behind רבי שמעון's position in the harp case, which ties it back to his rule 'only שבות was permitted.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bow can never become the מלאכה of קושר, so it is only a שבות, and the רבנן permitted it in the מקדש. A knot is the kind of act that can make a person liable for a חטאת, so it is more than a mere שבות. Since רבי שמעון holds the רבנן permitted only שבות, they did not permit a knot.

keyTerms.meaning: Tying a real knot (the מלאכה of קושר)
Being obligated to bring a sin-offering (a Torah-level violation)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון's single rule explains both rulings. The חכמים only relax rabbinic (שבות) prohibitions. So in the תחום case the extra fifteen אמות were truly allowed all along, and in the מקדש only a bow, never a Torah-level knot, is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: עֲנִיבָה, דְּלָא אָתֵי לִידֵי חִיּוּב חַטָּאת —
phrases.english: Forming a bow, which does not lead to liability for a sin-offering,
the Sages permitted it.
Tying a knot, which does lead to liability for a sin-offering,
the Sages did not permit it.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲנִיבָה, דְּלָא אָתֵי לִידֵי חִיּוּב חַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי שמעון's position given in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The line between bow and knot is the line between a rabbinic prohibition (permitted in the מקדש) and a Torah prohibition carrying a חטאת (not permitted).

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק המוצא תפילין and מסכת עירובין
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for פרק המוצא תפילין, and the announcement that מסכת עירובין is complete.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, 'המוצא תפילין,' and מסכת עירובין is finished.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional closing line. It ends the last פרק and the whole מסכת עירובין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new content is added. The הדרן expresses the learner's commitment to come back and review this פרק, and it marks the completion of the מסכת.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (the closing formula of a פרק)

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'One who finds tefillin'
and Tractate Eruvin is concluded

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formal closing after the final explanation of the משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פרק המוצא תפילין and מסכת עירובין are complete.
